name: rebind breaks alias
code:
a = [1]
b = a
b = [9]
print(a, b)

name: rebind source
code:
a = [1]
b = a
a = [2]
print(a, b)

name: two aliases mutate one
code:
a = [1]
b = a
c = a
b.append(2)
print(a, b, c)

name: alias then mutate via other
code:
a = [1]
b = a
a.append(2)
print(a, b)

name: alias of alias chain
code:
a = [1]
b = a
c = b
c.append(3)
print(a, b, c)

name: alias in function scope
code:
def f(x):
    y = x
    y.append(1)
a = []
f(a)
print(a)

name: nested alias
code:
a = [[1]]
b = a[0]
c = b
c.append(2)
print(a, b, c)

name: delete element via alias
code:
a = [1, 2]
b = a
del b[0]
print(a, b)

name: string is immutable
code:
s = 'x'
t = s
t = t + 'y'
print(s, t)
